texts.527326512450:
Objective for processing:  
RoSPA develops and delivers targeted accident prevention programmes based on data and best practice in order to ensure that it has the best chance of reducing the toll of unintentional injury on people’s lives and on services. 
The Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents (ROSPA) wish to further their understanding of the scale, causes and trends of hospital admission for external causes ICD codes V00 to Y99 in each local authority area of England. 
Unsuppressed data is required because in some individual areas the numbers are too small to register. Without the inclusion of small numbers it is not possible to gain a full picture of the scale of unintentional injury across the nation and assess the level of intervention required.
Safer Health Programme
RoSPA have utilised the HES data previously provided to target the Department of Health funded Safer Homes Programme and to ensure that RoSPA were working in the local authority areas that had the highest rates of hospital admissions. The updated HES data will enable RoSPA to conduct a further analysis of the areas that were targeted to examine progress in reducing accidents in these areas. 
Take Action Today Poisonings Programme. 
RoSPA are working with the local hospitals in relevant cities to evaluate this programme. The requested HES data will support this analysis. The programme will be launched in two further cities this year and the data will support the targeting, delivery and evaluation of these initiatives. 

Processing activities: 
Analysis of the HES data along with previous data supplied will be used to examine trends and key factors involved in admission. 
All processing activities will be undertaken by authorised staff that have a responsibility for data in their area of work within RoSPA, i.e., home safety/public health, road safety, leisure and water safety, occupational health and safety.
All processing activities will take place at RoSPA.
The outputs will be disseminated to public health professionals and those who have a commitment to reducing accidents to help target their work and to inform development of policy and strategy.

Specific outputs expected, including target date: 
The outputs (analysis and reports) will be disseminated to public health professionals and those who have a commitment to reducing accidents to help target their work and to inform development of policy and strategy. 
RoSPA works extensively with local authority public health departments and their partners to develop coherent accident prevention strategies and advice from RoSPA is often sought on the key priority areas. Where appropriate some of the analysis will be used in work on Public Health Priorities for Accident Prevention and the delivery of the Department of Health’s Safer Homes programme which is currently ongoing. RoSPA will be using this analysis to present at future conferences regarding this programme, to clinicians, commissioners and decision-makers within the NHS.
RoSPA will also use the information in general terms in public documents to raise awareness of a particular issue of concern or new issues emerging from the data. RoSPA can’t specify the precise subject matter of publication and dissemination without having first had an opportunity to analyse the data. As an example, being able to draw attention to an emerging issue with trampolining injuries following a close collaboration with one A&E department has enabled RoSPA to conduct significant awareness raising activity in national and local media that will hopefully contribute to a reduction in these needless (and sometimes life changing) accidents. Similar work has been undertaken with liquid detergent capsules, blind cords (supported by the Department for Business Innovation and Skills) and hair straighteners. The analysis of the data is not an academic exercise but one which will inform positive action to reduce accidents. 
All outputs will be either aggregated with small numbers suppressed in line with the HES analysis guide or generalised. An example of a generalised output would be results of admissions due to a particular accident published as an overall percentage compared to other types of accidents.

To be clear, no output will contain small numbers.
Target date: Quarter 1 2016.

Expected measurable benefits to health and/or social care including target date: 
From data previously provided RoSPA have been able to demonstrate the effectiveness of the Safe At Home National Home Safety Equipment Scheme (delivered for the Department for Education) in our top 10 Safe At Home areas. Data was also used to support the development of the handbook “Delivering Accident Prevention Effectively in the New Public Health System”(2012)  produced in conjunction with the Department of Health and Public Health England (available on the RoSPA website at http://www.rospa.com/public-health/ 
RoSPA have also used the data to target the Take Action Today Poisonings Programme which has seen information about how to prevent accidental poisoning delivered into over 100,000 homes across four cities targeted because of relatively high rates of admissions. RoSPA are working with the local hospitals in these cities to evaluate this programme and the requested data will support this analysis. The programme will be launched in two further cities in 2016 and the data will support the targeting, delivery and evaluation of these initiatives. The target data for the completion of this project is March 2017.
The last dataset provided was also used to target the Department of Health funded Safer Homes Programme and ensured that RoSPA were working in the local authority areas that had the highest rates of hospital admissions. A major part of the reason for this request has been to enable RoSPA to conduct a further analysis of the areas that were targeted to examine progress in reducing accidents in these areas.
